source.title: Complex Dynamics in Simple Neural Networks: Understanding Gradient Flow in Phase Retrieval
source.authors: Stefano Sarao Mannelli; G. Biroli; C. Cammarota; Florent Krzakala; Pierfrancesco Urbani; Lenka Zdeborov'a

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests gradient-flow success and failure in phase retrieval, a different task and model setting from the listed classification claims.
record.gate_note: The paper studies phase retrieval with a single-layer estimator and squared loss, not CIFAR classification. It reports training-loss outcomes and zero-test-error success rates for its own experiments. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports original phase-retrieval results, but none tests V1–V6. It varies samples per input dimension in a single-layer spherical estimator, measuring regression loss and signal recovery. It does not test convolutional classification, extra student neurons, depth, initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability thresholds, or normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors associate successful recovery with threshold states becoming unstable through a BBP-type Hessian transition. Their approximate 1RSB calculation predicts a transition near α = 13.8, while many finite-dimensional simulations succeed below approximately 7. They conjecture an order-one weak-recovery threshold, but leave the discrepancy and the infinite-dimensional limit unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Gradient flow on a spherical phase-retrieval objective with random sensing vectors and a single-layer estimator; not the classification-network recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with the number of samples per dimension α; finite-size effects shift the apparent transition.

fits_no_version.finding: At N = 16384, training loss remains nonzero at α = 6, recovery outcomes are mixed at α = 12, and training loss rapidly reaches zero at α = 18 and 24.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the studied spherical phase-retrieval objective, randomly initialized gradient flow can remain trapped at smaller sample-to-dimension ratios and recover the signal at larger ratios; the authors associate escape with a signal-aligned negative Hessian direction.

record.problems: The paper reports strong finite-size effects and says it is unclear whether the observed threshold will hold as input dimension tends to infinity. The 1RSB analysis is approximate, and the paper notes discrepancies from simulations. Figure 5 reports fractions of successful runs only graphically in the supplied text, so precise values are not extractable.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 reports success fractions for multiple input dimensions, but the supplied text gives no recoverable numeric values for those plotted points; no figure-only rows were added. Results for shuffled labels and Hessian spectra are not included as rows because they do not report the teacher-label recovery outcome measured in the retained rows.

untested.parts: All: convolutional classification training error on CIFAR, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe conditions.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and the effect of extra student neurons.
All: depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
All: initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, and trainable depth.

All: learning rates relative to stability thresholds and associated curvature and loss dynamics. Hessian measurements here concern a sample-ratio-dependent escape mechanism, not learning-rate stability.
All: batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification should be corrected: a new optimization setting alone does not test a listed version. All four rows describe legitimate results, but their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6. No additional result bearing on those versions is missing.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional classification on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted classification labels, and comparisons involving model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima by width, and student-teacher neuron-count differences.
Plain versus residual networks, depth, normalization, and the specified ImageNet/CIFAR or special-initialization settings.
Comparisons among initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth in the specified network architectures.
Learning-rate sweeps relative to a stability threshold, curvature or sharpness measurements, and the specified squared-loss wide-network settings.
Batch normalization comparisons, training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.
